edges.description: Mutant ATIC destabilizes assembly of the purinosome, the transient multienzyme complex of de novo purine synthesis enzymes.

nodes.description: Biallelic ATIC variants abolish or severely reduce the AICAR formyltransferase (transformylase) activity of the bifunctional enzyme, while the IMP cyclohydrolase activity is less affected. In the index patient's fibroblasts transformylase activity was profoundly deficient and cyclohydrolase activity was 40% of normal, and recombinant enzyme carrying the recurrent p.Lys426Arg substitution had no transformylase activity. Ramond et al. proposed that loss of transformylase activity causes a more severe phenotype than loss of cyclohydrolase activity.

genetic_context.description: Reported alleles include the recurrent missense p.Lys426Arg (c.1277A>G), which abolishes transformylase activity of the recombinant protein, frameshift and nonsense (p.Arg141Ter) alleles, a canonical splice-site variant (c.1321-2A>G), and missense p.Thr585Ala and p.Gln214His.

nodes.description: ZMP (AICAR) and its di- and triphosphates accumulate intracellularly, and AICA-riboside is excreted in large amounts in urine; succinyladenosine, a dephosphorylated intermediate from further up the same pathway, is also excreted in excess. This metabolite pattern is the biochemical hallmark and the diagnostic handle of the disorder.

nodes.description: ZMP activates AMP-activated protein kinase, a master regulator of cellular energy metabolism that suppresses mTOR-driven anabolic growth. ATIC-null HeLa cells accumulate ZMP without exogenous AICA-riboside and show transcriptome changes in neurodevelopmental, embryogenesis and cell-cycle genes. Whether AMPK is chronically activated in patient brain or retina has not been measured, so this node is a proposed route of toxicity rather than a demonstrated one.
